title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
subtitle: Neapolitan pasta with garlic, olive oil, and chilli
excerpt: The simplest pasta dish there is: spaghetti tossed with garlic slowly cooked in a great deal of good olive oil, finished with chilli and parsley. Ready in the time it takes to boil pasta.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spaghetti aglio e olio (spaghetti with garlic and oil) is a pasta dish from Naples with a long history as the dish made from almost nothing. It is part of the cucina povera tradition: a meal assembled from what is always in the house. The original dish was simply pasta with garlic-infused olive oil, made by fishermen and late-night revellers in Naples when nothing else was available. The chilli and parsley were later additions. In Italian cooking it is sometimes described as a mezzanotte (midnight) dish: made late at night with minimal ingredients. The technique requires patience with the garlic: it must be warmed in the olive oil slowly, over low heat, until it is golden and fragrant but not brown. Browned or burnt garlic is acrid and ruins the dish. The starchy pasta water is the crucial emulsifier that binds the oil and water into a light, glossy sauce that coats the pasta.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the pasta.

content.text: The garlic must be cooked over low heat, slowly, until it is pale gold: take it to the point where it just starts to colour and then watch it carefully. A few seconds too long and it burns. Reserve a generous amount of the starchy pasta cooking water before draining: it is the emulsifier that turns the oil and water into a sauce that clings to the pasta. Add it in stages to the drained pasta with the oil and toss vigorously until the sauce is creamy and glossy.

items.preparation: deseeded and finely sliced; or a pinch of dried chilli flakes

content.text: Cook the pasta in generously salted boiling water until 1 minute before done. While the pasta cooks, put the garlic and olive oil in a large, wide pan over the lowest possible heat. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the garlic is pale gold. Add the chilli for the final 2 minutes.

Reserve 200 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain the pasta. Add the pasta and half the reserved water to the pan with the oil. Increase the heat to medium. Toss vigorously for 1 to 2 minutes, adding more water as needed, until the sauce is emulsified and glossy.
Remove from the heat, scatter over the parsley, and toss again. Serve immediately in warm bowls. No cheese is served with this dish in the traditional Neapolitan style.
